items.basis: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION mix (per kg charged): 45% nodular pig Q10 (2.796) + 30% steel scrap (2.045) + 25% returns valued at the charge's own cost -> metallics = (0.45x2.796 + 0.30x2.045)/0.75 = 2.496; + FeSiMg 1.3% x 9.071 (rare-earth FeSi PROXY) = 0.118; + inoculant 0.4% x 5.442 (FeSi75 as proxy; Ba/Ca inoculants cost more) = 0.022; / 0.98 melt & treatment loss = 2.689 CNY/kg ex-VAT.
items.notes: Excludes carburiser (not priced), Cu/Sn pearlite additions for 500-7 (Cu from the non-ferrous research: ~0.3% Cu adds ~0.25 CNY/kg at ~85 CNY/kg Cu - not researched here), and the foundry-grade scrap premium over HMS. Ex-works prices, delivery not added.

items.basis: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION mix (induction grey iron): 25% foundry pig Z18 (2.611) + 40% steel scrap (2.045) + 35% returns at charge cost -> (0.25x2.611 + 0.40x2.045)/0.65 = 2.263; + FeSi75 0.5% Si trim + 0.2% inoculant = 0.7% x 5.442 = 0.038; / 0.98 melt loss = 2.348 CNY/kg ex-VAT.
items.notes: Excludes carburiser (needed with 40% steel scrap; not priced) and bought cast-iron scrap (no China price found - the UK book's 60% cast-iron-scrap mix cannot be priced in China). A cupola/higher-pig mix (e.g. 50% pig) gives ~2.5.

items.basis: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION: 70% steel scrap (2.045) + 30% returns at charge cost -> metallics 2.045; + FeSi75 0.5% x 5.442 = 0.027 deoxidation/Si; / 0.96 melt loss (steel) = 2.159 CNY/kg ex-VAT.
items.notes: Excludes FeMn (Mn 0.5-0.8%; not researched), Al wire, and the clean-scrap premium over HMS - so a floor. Also applies to G20Mn5 / A216 WCB as a base.

items.basis: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION, scrap route (usual for a CF8 foundry): 80% 304 industrial scrap (8.363) + 20% returns at charge cost -> 8.363; / 0.97 melt loss = 8.622 CNY/kg ex-VAT. Virgin-alloy upper bound: Fe 70% steel scrap (2.045) + Cr 19% at 13.80/kg Cr (HC FeCr) + Ni 9% at 115.619 = (1.432 + 2.622 + 10.406)/0.97 = 14.91.
items.notes: Scrap route excludes small Cr/Ni trims and decarburisation (AOD) for CF8 C<=0.08; the virgin bound understates Cr (HC FeCr is too high in carbon; low-C FeCr costs more). Range 8.6 - 14.9; Mysteel says 304 scrap is cheaper per Ni unit than NPI, so the scrap route is the market basis.
